title: BEAST v1.X Tutorial: Mammalian Timetree
author: kawaoso
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.brdym27w
materials: Trees: Tree Prior: Speciation: Yule Process.
MCMC: Length of chain: 10,000,000. Default setting.

steps.title: Install BEAGLE library
steps.instruction: Download and install the BEAGLE Library required for BEAST v1.X before running any BEAST analyses.

steps.title: Prepare mitochondrial dataset
steps.instruction: Obtain whole mitochondrial sequences from GenBank/DDBJ, align them with ClustalW in MEGA X, exclude all gapped non‑protein‑coding regions, and save the resulting protein‑coding alignment (total length = 10,112 bp) as a plain‑text (.txt) file.

steps.title: Launch BEAUti (BEAST v1.X)
steps.instruction: Start BEAUti, which is part of BEAST v1.X (released 10 June 2018).

steps.title: Load alignment and partitions
steps.instruction: In BEAUti, load the .txt alignment file using the “+” button; the same button is used to add any additional partition files if required.

steps.title: Define taxa set
steps.instruction: Load the taxa list via the “+” button, then in the left panel check the “Monophyletic” box for every taxon and check the “Stem” box for Erinaceidae, Theria, and Prototheria; the right panel will display the included taxa.

steps.title: Set substitution model
steps.instruction: Select the HKY (Hasegawa‑Kishino‑Yano) model for the site substitution settings.

steps.title: Configure clock model
steps.instruction: Choose an uncorrected relaxed clock with a log‑normal relaxed distribution; note that each branch may have its own rate and the node rate is taken as the median of the three descendant branches.

steps.title: Enter calibration priors (tMRCA)
steps.instruction: For each calibration point (A–S) input the fossil or geological age as a Normal prior with the mean equal to the reported age and the standard deviation equal to the reported uncertainty.

substeps.instruction: Calibration A – 0.545 ± 0.003 Ma (Ar‑Ar, East African Rift chimpanzee).
Calibration B – 8.072 ± 0.8 Ma (Ar‑Ar + magnetostratigraphy, East African Rift gorilla).
Calibration D – 24.93 ± 0.49 Ma (U‑Pb, Nsungwe Formation, Tanzania).
Calibration H – 51.96 ± 4.6 Ma (Yepresian, Indian fossil horizon, leporid/ochotonid ancestor).
Calibration J – 10.4 Ma (magneto‑stratigraphic, Pakistan, Mus‑Rattus divergence).
Calibration K – 51.25 ± 0.31 Ma (weighted average of 53.5‑48.5 Ma, Ar‑Ar, Green River Formation Orohippus).
Calibration M – 53.25 ± 0.75 Ma (planktonic foraminifer zone, Pakistan, Artiodactyla).
Calibration N – 18.205 ± 2.235 Ma (Burdigalian, Siwalik Deposits, Bovinae‑Antilopinae).
Calibration P – 57.6 ± 1.6 Ma (Thanetian, Morocco Eritherium, Afrotheria).
Calibration Q – 51.96 ± 4.6 Ma (Yepresian, Australia Djarthia, Marsupialia).
Calibration R – 160.7 ± 0.4 Ma (Ar‑Ar, Liaoning Juramaia sinensis, Theria).
Calibration S – 162.7 ± 1.1 Ma (Bathonian, Madagascar Ambondro mahabo, Mammalia).

steps.title: Run BEAST analysis
steps.instruction: Start the BEAST run; the analysis typically requires more than 2 hours of CPU time (5 hours were needed for the dataset described here).

steps.title: Summarize trees with TreeAnnotator
steps.instruction: Load the BEAST output tree files into TreeAnnotator to generate a summarized (maximum clade credibility) tree.

steps.title: Visualize tree in FigTree
steps.instruction: Open the summarized tree in FigTree v1.4.2; display the 95 % highest posterior density (HPD) intervals, posterior probabilities, node ages, and the rate‑median values.
